evidence.note: Started the service and ran real HTTP verification: health checks on all three ports, register/login, workspace/channel/message creation, cross-node reads/writes, message edit, and reactions via curl — beyond pure happy-path single endpoints.
Planned to smoke-test IRC and file behavior after patching PRIVMSG and file attachments, showing intent to exercise the IRC subsystem, but the test was never actually executed.
Restart health probe failed; agent then burned ~11 steps trying to recover a stuck terminal (Ctrl-C/D/U/Z) and never re-verified the patched build; the IRC/file smoke test never ran.

Submitted complete without ever testing WebSocket subscribe/resume/seq, an actual IRC session, the SPA in a browser, seq-density under mixed writers, or any SIGKILL/broadcast-kill resilience scenario — all assumed to work.

reasoning: The agent did more than a couple of happy-path curls: it verified HTTP status/envelope behavior across all three nodes plus edits and reactions, showing some cross-node awareness (above anchor 3). But it never exercised a WebSocket subscribe, never completed an IRC join/privmsg session, never drove the SPA, and never touched seq-density or the resilience/broadcast-kill probes — the WS/IRC/SPA main-path coverage required for anchor 5 is missing, and resilience was fully assumed. That places it between the 3 and 5 anchors, at 4.
